title: Local mate law for componentwise direct-image transitions
statement: For a componentwise direct-image datum D from [lem-coef-ordinary-direct-system-core-components] whose horizontal maps are normalized to uPush of the original maps, and an ordinary inverse system as in [lem-coef-ordinary-inverse-system], assume the supplied set-sheaf and normalized module adjunctions of [lem-coef-normalized-module-adjunction]. The horizontal square of any two component maps of systems of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models] commutes if and only if the horizontal square of their levelwise adjunction transposes commutes.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03D7, direct images of modules and the adjunction transpose, applied levelwise to strict sequence-site systems.

proof.text: Conjugate the two inverse-image component maps by P.component and I.moduleUnderlying. P.transition followed by P.restriction_underlying and naturality identifies the horizontal inverse-image edge with uInv of the source transition.

Conjugate the two direct-image maps by D.component and eV. The explicit normalization of D identifies its horizontal edge with uPush of the target transition. The assumed normalized Hom equations identify the component transposes with the set-sheaf adjunction transposes. Naturality and injectivity of that Hom equivalence give equivalence of the two squares; faithfulness of the underlying functors reflects both equalities.

theorem ordinaryDirectSystem_core_transition_mate_exists [PreservesFiniteLimits uInv]
    (_hI : ∀ n,
      uInv.map ((sheafCompose J (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{max c v r})).map (τ n)) ≫
          (I n).ringUnderlying.hom =
        (I (n + 1)).ringUnderlying.hom ≫
          (sheafCompose J' (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{max c v r})).map (σ n))
    (uPush : Sheaf J' (Type (max c v r)) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type (max c v r)))
    (adjSet : uInv ⊣ uPush)
    (eV : ∀ n, V n ⋙ underlying.{c, v, r} J (B n) ≅
      underlying.{c, v, r} J' (F n) ⋙ uPush)
    (ha : ∀ n (M : Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n))
      (N : Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' (F n)) (f : (I n).modules.obj M ⟶ N),
      (underlying.{c, v, r} J (B n)).map ((a n).homEquiv M N f) ≫ (eV n).hom.app N =
        adjSet.homEquiv _ _ ((I n).moduleUnderlying.inv.app M ≫
          (underlying.{c, v, r} J' (F n)).map f))
    (D : OrdinaryDirectSystemCoreData.{c, v, r} (J := J) (B := B) (τ := τ)
      (J' := J') (F := F) (σ := σ) (V := V))
    (hD : OrdinaryDirectSystemCoreNormalized.{c, v, r} J B τ J' F σ V D uPush eV) :
    OrdinaryDirectSystemCoreTransitionMate.{c, v, r} (J := J) (B := B) (τ := τ)
      (J' := J') (F := F) (σ := σ) (I := I) (P := P) (V := V) (a := a) (D := D)

statement_change.old_statement: For any componentwise direct-image datum from `lem-coef-ordinary-direct-system-core-components`, the supplied coefficient compatibility, ordinary inverse-system transition equation, set-sheaf adjunction and normalized level adjunction imply the local mate equivalence: for every pair of systems, indices `n ≤ m`, and component maps at `m` and `n`, the source horizontal square commutes exactly when the square for their levelwise transposes commutes.
statement_change.what: STATEMENT-DISPUTED (former assertion): component data alone do not determine horizontal maps. On the one-object site with a constant nonzero ring and identity adjoints, the functor retaining levels and replacing every strict transition between distinct indices by zero has identity component isomorphisms. The two identity component maps of a constant tower satisfy the source square, while their transposes would require zero = identity. Add the actual horizontal normalization of D; its existence is proved in the components node.
